name: Nemesis

global_influences.evidence: Available sources document Nemesis's formation and hit singles but do not specify concrete Western artist or genre influences; flagged for further research (e.g., band interviews) rather than assumed.

local_adaptation_notes: Formed by recent high-school graduates with abundant free time, Nemesis's origin story — meeting future vocalist Zohad at a New Year's Eve rooftop party — reflects the informal, peer-network-driven formation pattern common to late-1990s/early-2000s Dhaka youth bands, later professionalizing via G-Series (debut album) and Dead Line Music (second album) label releases.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (1999–2000): formed by high-school-age friends; vocalist Zohad Reza Chowdhury joined in early 2000 after a chance rooftop-party meeting. Breakthrough period (2005): debut album Onneshon (G-Series) produced enduring hits 'Obocheton' and 'Kolporajjo,' propelling the band to mainstream popularity through the late 2000s and early 2010s. Consolidation period (2011): second album Tritio Jatra (Dead Line Music) added further hits ('Bir,' 'Kobe') to the band's catalogue across a three-studio-album career to date.
concert_culture_notes: Co-headlined the BAMBA Eid celebration concert at Jamuna Future Park alongside Warfaze, Maqsood O Dhaka, Renaissance and Mechanix (see data/concerts/bamba-eid-concert-jamuna-future-park.json), indicating an active presence within the multi-band festival circuit typical of mainstream Bangladeshi rock acts.
listener_community_notes: One of the most popular mainstream/alternative rock bands of the late 2000s–early 2010s generation, appealing to listeners bridging the earlier 'Big Three' rock era and the newer alternative/indie scene.
